title: The Tree in Vertical Slices

concept.title: Give every node a column and a row, then group by column
body: Draw the tree on a grid: the root is in column 0, a left child is one column to the left of its parent, a right child one column to the right; the row is the depth. The *vertical order* lists the nodes column by column, from the leftmost column to the rightmost one. Inside one column the nodes are listed from top to bottom, and two nodes in the same row and column are listed in increasing order of their values.

The traversal can visit the nodes in any order, because the final sort by `(row, value)` puts every column in the required order. Separating "collect the facts" (column, row, value) from "decide the output order" (sort) keeps the code simple.

statement: Place a binary tree on a grid: the root is in column 0 and row 0; the left child of a node in column `c` and row `r` is in column `c - 1` and row `r + 1`; the right child is in column `c + 1` and row `r + 1`. Print the values column by column, from the leftmost column to the rightmost one. Inside a column list the values from the top row to the bottom row, and when two values are in the same row, in increasing order. Every column is one line: the number of its values, then the values.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: One line for every column, from left to right: the number of values in the column, then the values from top to bottom.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The columns are 9 | 3 15 | 20 | 7, so the lines are "1 9", "2 3 15", "1 20" and "1 7".

hints: Walk the tree and remember the column and the row of every node.
Collect (row, value) pairs for each column.
Sort the columns from left to right and the pairs of a column by row and then by value.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def vertical(root):
    # Your code here: return a list with one list of values for every column, from left to right
    return []

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

for column in vertical(build_tree(vals)):
    print(len(column), *column)

explanation: A walk records for each node its column, row and value; the columns are then taken from left to right and the cells of each column sorted by row and by value.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).
